REV-1 [R5] R5 requires dialogs that are not shown to be lazy-loaded, and its pitfall says 'Do not load the git tools, console or dialogs as part of the initial view'. Here only one dialog body (ThemeFinder) plus the palette are split; the other eight modal dialogs remain in the initial bundle. Move the dialog bodies (at least Help, UpdateDialog and the big texts) into lazy modules rendered under Suspense so the initial view does not carry them.

REV-2 [R1] R1's pitfall forbids relying on source reading alone: the plan must be checked against the running app, including the real on-screen look and the CSS, before/with the window change. Do the running-app pass (or record what was actually observed on screen) instead of deferring it to a later merge gate.
REV-3 [R1] Merge BranchMenu into a single plan entry (noting its dialog role there) so the inventory is unique and a reviewer can trace it to exactly one entry.
REV-4 [USR-006] Add up/down/enter selection and keep focus inside the modal so the VS Code-style palette is efficient from the keyboard (USR-006 §2.1 keyboard navigation / §5.8 accessibility).
REV-5 [R5] Reset the tools state when the app/repository changes (e.g. key GitBar by app id, or an effect) if every app view should start collapsed.
REV-6 [R3] Assert the layout behaviour the test names (e.g. the header has flex-wrap and the groups keep min-width:0 in TopBar.module.css) rather than only the DOM parent.

QA-1 [R5] R5 acceptance 'Parts that are not shown are loaded when needed rather than up front, so the initial view does not carry them' has no test that can fail: the new code-splitting of GitDrawer/ConsoleNav/EditPane/ThemeFinder/CommandPalette is unproven, and the Help/Update dialogs are still in the initial chunk.

QA-2 [R1] The plan puts the branch popover in both the panel (P9) and dialog (D10) inventories, and the R1 test cannot notice a part appearing more than once, so the 'exactly one place' acceptance is both unproven and currently false.

QA-3 [R3] The R3 edge case 'the grouped top bar stays usable at the window sizes the app supports without controls overlapping or clipping' is asserted only structurally; the assertion cannot detect clipping. The wrap rules are present in the CSS, but the test does not prove them.
QA-4 [R4] The R4 Ctrl+O conflict edge case is only half covered: the 'shortcut is not added' half is tested, the 'plan records the conflict and the chosen alternative' half is not.

QA-5 [R5] R5's edge cases 'a part needed while something happens elsewhere, such as console output arriving, stays reachable' and 'the plan says how many steps it takes and where the entry sits' are not covered by a test.
